meta.description: Integrate learned routing into ruflo hooks

user.t:
You are the RUFLO INTEGRATION engineer. Context: ruflo (claude-flow v3) is installed in the repo C:\Users\mariu\howler-agents (git branch `neural-mesh-router`; do not switch branches, do not commit). Its hook layer lives in C:\Users\mariu\howler-agents\.claude\helpers\ — router.cjs (keyword task->agent router that prints the "Routing task ... Primary Recommendation" box on every prompt), hook-handler.cjs (dispatches hooks: route, post-edit, post-task, session-*), intelligence.cjs, learning-*.  The hooks are wired in .claude/settings.json. We are building a Hebbian-routed agent mesh (contract: C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\DESIGN.md — read the HebbianRouter, NeuralMesh and CLI sections). Another agent is concurrently building the `neural-mesh` CLI binary there (cargo; binary will be at C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\target\release\neural-mesh.exe or target\debug\neural-mesh.exe once built).

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- These hooks run on EVERY user prompt of a live Claude Code session. Any exception, slowness (>200 ms added) or changed stdout when disabled would break the user's session. New behaviour must be OFF by default, enabled only by env var NEURAL_MESH_ROUTER=1 (and optional NEURAL_MESH_BIN path), wrapped so any error/timeout falls back silently to the existing keyword result.
- Do NOT edit .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json, or any file outside .claude/helpers/ and a new test folder (e.g. .claude/helpers/__tests__/ or tests/neural-mesh-hooks/). Make a backup copy (*.bak-neural-mesh) of every helper file before editing it.
- Do not run ruflo/claude-flow init, upgrade, daemons, or npx installs.

Tasks:
1. Read router.cjs, hook-handler.cjs, intelligence.cjs and summarise exactly how a task is routed today, what feedback (if any) post-task records, and where outcomes could come from (hooks_post-task success flag, TaskCompleted hook, etc.). Report file:line.
2. Implement a learned-routing layer: when enabled, route() calls `neural-mesh route --state <.claude-flow/neural-mesh/state.json> --features <keywords from the prompt> --candidates <ruflo agent list>` (spawnSync with a short timeout), and uses its agent as the primary recommendation (keep the keyword result as fallback and show both in the box only when enabled). post-task / TaskCompleted calls `neural-mesh feedback ... --reward` with success->1, failure->0. Feature extraction must reuse router.cjs's existing keyword tokenisation.
3. Until the real binary exists, test against a tiny fake CLI you write in the test folder (node script emitting the same JSON contract). Tests (plain node, no npm installs): disabled => output identical to before (compare against the original module's output for a set of prompts); enabled + fake binary => uses learned agent; enabled + missing/slow/crashing binary => falls back to keyword with no exception and bounded latency; feedback call issued on post-task. Measure added latency.
4. If the real binary appears (check target\release or target\debug), rerun the enabled tests against it.

Final report (concise): how routing works today (file:line), files changed (with backups), how to enable, test results incl. latency, and any risk you see.

handback.t:
Learned routing is built and its tests pass, but it never runs in your current live session. This session has `RUFLO_MODS_OWNS=route,post-edit` set. That makes `hook-handler.cjs route` return immediately, because the ruflo-mods plugin (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/ruflo/ruflo-mods/0.1.0/hooks/route/`) routes in-process with its own copy of the keyword router. So the "Routing task … Primary Recommendation" box you see comes from that plugin, not from `hook-handler.cjs`. I tried to make `route` run anyway when the mesh is enabled, but that edit was refused by the auto-mode classifier as self-modification, and I did not try another way. You need to pick one of these:
- **Disable the ruflo-mods plugin.** Then the hook-handler route path runs again.
- **Approve the one-line override** in `main()`: `if (ownedByMod(command) && !(command === 'route' && neuralMesh)) return;`. The plugin's keyword box would still be added to the prompt as well.

Until then, post-task finds no route to give a reward to, so it does nothing.

## How routing works today (line numbers are from the unedited backup)
- **Hook wiring** (`.claude/settings.json`): UserPromptSubmit runs `route` (:54), PostToolUse Write/Edit runs `post-edit` (:43), and both TeammateIdle (:144) and TaskCompleted (:155) run `post-task`.
- **`router.cjs`**:
  - `TASK_PATTERNS` (:30-45) are compiled by `buildPattern` (:54-64) into word-boundary regexes.
  - `routeTask` (:72-91) returns the first pattern that matches, in table order, with a fixed confidence of 0.6. With no match it returns `coder` at 0.3.
  - Nothing is learned.
- **`hook-handler.cjs`**:
  - `ownedByMod` check: :294-298, called at :326.
  - The prompt comes from stdin `prompt`, then env, then argv (:357-358).
  - The `route` handler (:380-455) prints `intelligence.getContext` (:382-387), then the box from `routeTask` (:389-400).
  - `pre-task` re-routes but only logs (:552-563).
- **What post-task records** (:565-575): it calls `intelligence.feedback(!toolFailed)`. That only changes the confidence of the memory patterns `getContext` last matched (`intelligence.cjs:602-657`, `feedback` :691-697, +0.05 / -0.02 via `boostConfidence` :699-729). Which agent was routed is never recorded or rewarded.
- **Where outcomes come from:** only `toolFailed` (:365-377), which looks for `is_error`, `success:false`, a non-zero exit code or an error string in the tool result. TaskCompleted and TeammateIdle payloads usually carry no tool result, so they almost always count as success.

## Files changed (nothing committed, still on `neural-mesh-router`)
- **`.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs`**, backed up as `hook-handler.cjs.bak-neural-mesh` first. Three changes:
  - The new module is loaded only when `NEURAL_MESH_ROUTER` is truthy.
  - In `route`, a learned result becomes the primary recommendation with the keyword result shown under it. Any failure prints the unchanged keyword box.
  - `post-task` calls `recordFeedback(!toolFailed)` and prints nothing extra.
- **New: `.claude/helpers/neural-mesh-router.cjs`**:
  - Features come from router.cjs's own `TASK_PATTERNS` and `buildPattern`, but every matched token is used rather than only the first. A prompt with no match gets the feature `no-keyword`.
  - Candidates are `Object.keys(AGENT_CAPABILITIES)`.
  - The CLI is called with `spawnSync` and a timeout. It falls back to keyword routing if the binary is missing, slow, crashes, prints bad JSON, or names an agent that isn't a candidate.
  - Each route is saved to `last-route.json` and rewarded at most once; an atomic rename stops two post-task hooks from both rewarding it. Routes older than 6 hours are ignored.
  - Errors go to `.claude-flow/neural-mesh/errors.log`, capped at 256 KB.
- **New: `.claude/helpers/__tests__/neural-mesh/fake-neural-mesh.cjs`**: a stand-in CLI that follows the same JSON contract and can simulate slow, crash, garbage, unknown-agent and hung-feedback failures.
- **New: `.claude/helpers/__tests__/neural-mesh/run-tests.cjs`**: plain node, run in a temp sandbox so your live `.claude-flow` data is never touched.
- `router.cjs`, `intelligence.cjs` and `settings.json` are untouched.

## How to enable
Set these in the environment Claude Code is launched from (or in your settings `env`, which I did not edit). It only takes effect once the ruflo-mods issue above is resolved.
- `NEURAL_MESH_ROUTER=1`
- `NEURAL_MESH_BIN=C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\target\release\neural-mesh.exe` (or the debug build)
- Optional: `NEURAL_MESH_STATE` (default `<project>/.claude-flow/neural-mesh/state.json`)
- Optional: `NEURAL_MESH_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 150, allowed range 10–1000)

## Test results
Run with `node .claude/helpers/__tests__/neural-mesh/run-tests.cjs`.
- **Fake CLI:** all 13 tests pass.
  - With the mesh off, `route` and `post-task` output is byte-identical to the backup for 11 prompts, including empty, unicode and 5,000-character prompts. The CLI is never called and no state folder is created.
  - With the mesh on and a trained mesh, the learned agent (`reviewer`) is shown first and `coder` appears under "Keyword Fallback".
  - With a missing, slow (3 s against a 150 ms timeout), crashing, garbage-printing or unknown-agent CLI, output is identical to keyword-only and nothing throws.
  - Post-task sends exactly one feedback call per route (success gives `--reward 1`, failure `--reward 0`), a second post-task sends nothing, and a hung feedback call is cut off.
- **Real binary:** `target\debug\neural-mesh.exe` appeared, so I reran with `NM_REAL_BIN` set. All 8 tests that don't depend on the fake's fault injection pass (5 skipped). Its JSON (`{agent, team, scores:{…}, health, features}`) matches what the hook expects.

| Latency (ms) | Fake CLI | Real debug binary |
|---|---|---|
| Route hook, original (median) | 49.0 | 42.5 |
| Route hook, new code, mesh off (median) | 47.7 | 42.1 (no added cost) |
| Route hook, mesh on (median) | 103 | 134 |
| Learned call alone (median / max) | 55.6 / 127.6 | 91.9 / 93.9 |
| Fallback, missing binary | 3.4 | 2.5 |
| Fallback, slow binary | 159 | — |

## Risks
1. The ruflo-mods ownership problem above. This is the blocker.
2. The debug binary takes about 92 ms against the 150 ms default timeout. Under load it can time out and quietly fall back to keyword routing. Use a release build or raise `NEURAL_MESH_TIMEOUT_MS`.
3. The reward signal is weak. It is almost always 1, it isn't tied to whether Claude actually used the recommended agent, and when several tasks complete per prompt only the first one counts.
4. The state file is written by separate processes (route and feedback, possibly from parallel subagents). The CLI does not lock it, so updates can be lost.
5. When enabled, the agent list is router.cjs's 8 agents only, not the full ruflo agent catalogue.
